meta.title: In Spring — Set 5
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Challenge quiz for 'In Spring' — opinion text features, inference, and theme.

questions.question: Why is 'In Spring' considered an opinion text rather than just a fact text?
options: Because it has no real facts about plants or animals.
Because the author tries to persuade the reader that spring is the best season.
Because the author actually prefers the winter season.
Because it is a story about a magic squirrel.
questions.explanation: The text contains facts, but the main goal of the author is to persuade the reader of their opinion: that 'Spring is the best season.'

questions.question: The author uses words like 'warmer' and 'longer' to show that spring days are getting better.
questions.explanation: True. Comparative words like 'warmer' and 'longer' support the opinion that spring is a pleasant and good season.

questions.question: Why does the author mention fawns struggling to walk on young legs?
options: To show that spring can be a sad or dangerous season for animals.
To show that spring is a special season when new baby animals are born.
To explain that baby deer cannot walk at all.
To warn readers not to walk in the woods.
questions.explanation: Baby animals are a key reason why people like spring. Showing a fawn learning to walk highlights the new life in spring.

questions.question: In the text, 'breezes blow hints of hotter days' means that summer weather is already here.
questions.explanation: False. 'Hints' means signs or clues. The breezes show that summer is coming soon, but it is still spring.

questions.question: Why can children run outside after dinner without a coat in spring?
options: Because it gets dark very early in the afternoon.
Because spring days are longer and warmer than winter days.
Because parents do not care what they wear.
Because it only rains in the morning.
questions.explanation: Longer days mean there is still light after dinner, and warmer weather means a heavy coat isn't needed.

questions.question: The author says that spring _______ the cold of winter with the heat of summer.
questions.explanation: Spring connects (links) the two opposite seasons: cold winter and hot summer.

questions.question: Which animal action shows that spring weather is getting warmer and ice is disappearing?
options: Squirrels darting in trees.
Tadpoles swimming beneath melting ice.
Worms coiling in dry grass.
Fawns learning to run.
questions.explanation: Tadpoles swimming under 'melting ice' shows the winter ice is turning back to warm water.

questions.question: Sort these sentences from the story into Facts (can be proven) or Opinions (feelings/beliefs):
questions.explanation: Day length and animal births can be measured (facts). Calling a season 'the best' or 'most fun' is a personal belief (opinion).

questions.question: The question 'Don't you think so too?' is meant to make the reader agree with the author.
questions.explanation: True. The author asks this question to encourage the reader to agree that spring is the best season.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show what spring does to winter:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'Spring waves good-bye to winter.' This means the cold season is leaving.

questions.question: How do spring flowers 'hide' behind trees in the woods?
options: They move when they hear footsteps.
They grow close to tree trunks, which blocks them from view.
They only open their petals at night.
The wind cover them up with snow.
questions.explanation: Flowers grow on the forest floor, often nestled behind tree trunks, requiring you to walk in the woods to 'spy' (notice) them.

questions.question: A baby frog swimming in the pond is a _______, while a baby deer is a fawn.
questions.explanation: Tadpoles are baby frogs, and fawns are baby deer. Both are signs of spring.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show how spring connects seasons:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'It links winter with summer.' 'It' refers to the spring season.

questions.question: Plants start growing in spring because winter temperatures are rising and days have more sunlight.
questions.explanation: True. The warm weather and longer daylight hours trigger plants to grow again.

questions.question: How does spring 'wave good-bye' to the winter season?
options: By making the weather colder and blowing red leaves.
By melting pond ice, warming the days, and letting animals come outside.
By causing animals to start hibernating.
By bringing dry winds and heat waves.
questions.explanation: As temperatures rise, snow/ice melt and animals wake up, showing that the cold winter is officially over (waving good-bye).
